_meta.indication: Lexiscan is a pharmacologic stress agent indicated for radionuclide myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) in patients unable to undergo adequate exercise stress.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy multicenter non-inferiority trial comparing Lexiscan to adenosine as a pharmacologic stress agent for SPECT MPI
pivotal_trials.population: Males and females greater than 18 years old with a clinical indication (such as chest pain) for a pharmacological stress SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging study, who tolerated a baseline adenosine injection
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Non-inferiority of the agreement between Lexiscan and adenosine images versus the agreement between two sequential adenosine images, based on number of segments with reversible defects (prespecified lower bound of 95% CI = -13%)
pivotal_trials.result: Met primary endpoint: adenosine-regadenoson agreement rate 62 ± 2% vs adenosine-adenosine agreement 61 ± 3%; rate difference (R - A) 1 ± 4%, 95% CI -8 to 9% (within prespecified -13% margin)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy multicenter non-inferiority trial, identical in design to CVT 5131, comparing Lexiscan to adenosine
pivotal_trials.population: Males and females greater than 18 years old with a clinical indication (such as chest pain) for a pharmacological stress SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging study, who tolerated a baseline adenosine injection
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Non-inferiority of the agreement between Lexiscan and adenosine images versus two sequential adenosine images (prespecified lower bound of 95% CI = -13%)
pivotal_trials.result: Met primary endpoint: adenosine-regadenoson agreement rate 63 ± 3% vs adenosine-adenosine agreement 64 ± 4%; rate difference (R - A) -1 ± 5%, 95% CI -11 to 9% (within prespecified -13% margin)

key_safety: Most common (incidence ≥5%) adverse reactions: dyspnea (28%), headache (26%), flushing (16%), chest discomfort (13%), angina pectoris or ST segment depression (12%), dizziness (8%), chest pain (7%), nausea (6%); serious risks include myocardial ischemia/cardiac arrest, SA/AV nodal block, hypotension, and bronchoconstriction
target_moa: Regadenoson is a low-affinity A2A adenosine receptor agonist; activation of the A2A adenosine receptor produces coronary vasodilation and increases coronary blood flow

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the product is a member of the class of previously approved pharmacologic agents (adenosine injection) and molecularly similar to adenosine

description.text: Added use as a pharmacologic stress agent for radionuclide myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) in patients unable to undergo adequate exercise stress

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application proposes use of LEXISCAN® (regadenoson) as a pharmacologic stress agent for radionuclide myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) in patients unable to undergo adequate exercise stress.

basis.text: The NDA was assigned a standard (not priority) review at the June 26, 2007 filing meeting.

summary.text: Standard (non-priority) 505(b) NDA review approved first cycle on April 10, 2008 without referral to an advisory committee, based on two Phase 3 non-inferiority trials versus adenosine; no accelerated approval or special designations, with two required postmarketing clinical trials in bronchoconstrictive disease and chronic kidney disease.

citations.quote: • May 14, 2007 - submission of NDA• June 26, 2007 - filing meeting, NDA was assigned a standard review• July 27, 2007 - filing date• October 29, 2007 - mid-cycle meeting• March 14, 2008 - PDUFA due date
Your application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee for the following reasons.
The sponsor utilized two Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy multicenter trials to demonstrate the non-inferiority of Lexiscan when compared to adenosine as a psa.

Therefore, based on appropriate scientific data, FDA has determined that you are required, pursuant to section 505(o)(3) of the Act, to conduct the following postmarketing clinical trials of Lexiscan:

requirement.text: A clinical trial to examine the pulmonary adverse effects of a single 0.4 mg dose of Lexiscan in approximately 600 patients with a broad severity of bronchoconstrictive disease (300 with asthma, 300 with COPD), with follow-up for at least 24 hours after administration (required under 505(o)(3)).

citations.quote: A clinical trial to examine the pulmonary adverse effects of a single 0.4mg dose of Lexiscan in approximately 600 patients with a broad severity of bronchoconstrictive disease (300 with asthma, 300 with COPD). Patient follow-up for the detection of adverse reactions will extend over a time period of at least 24 hours following Lexiscan administration.

requirement.text: A clinical trial to examine the serious adverse effects of a single 0.4 mg dose of Lexiscan in approximately 300 patients with moderate (or worse) chronic kidney disease (Stage 3 or greater), with follow-up for at least 24 hours after administration (required under 505(o)(3)).

citations.quote: A clinical trial to examine the serious adverse effects of a single 0.4mg dose of Lexiscan in approximately 300 patients with moderate (or worse) chronic kidney disease (Stage 3 or greater/using NKF GFR definitions). Patient follow-up for the detection of adverse reactions will extend over a time period of at least 24 hours following Lexiscan administration.
